requirements.requirement: Provide the supplied documents as a WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Apache was observed running and listening on TCP 8080. Authenticated GET and PROPFIND against /documents/ succeeded both before and after reboot, and the supplied document names were present.

requirements.requirement: Allow the editor account from access.txt to create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: A direct authenticated test successfully created, read, replaced, reread, and deleted a temporary document. Post-restart testing again demonstrated authenticated reads, creation, and deletion.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive document locks so an update without the lock token cannot overwrite a locked document.
requirements.summary: LOCK succeeded, a tokenless PUT returned HTTP 423, and token-authorized update plus UNLOCK succeeded. The same behavior was demonstrated after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Prevent anonymous clients from accessing the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous GET and PROPFIND returned HTTP 401 before reboot, and anonymous access still returned 401 after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: The original brief.txt and budget.csv were present before configuration, retained matching pre-change and post-restart checksums, and remained in the required source tree after functional tests and reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after implementation and reboot. The installed Apache 2.2.3 package was sourced from CentOS 5 repositories and operated successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for node1: healthy pre-restart service and data were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and service, documents, authentication, CRUD behavior, and lock enforcement recovered after reboot.
limitations: The fixed after-executor listening-socket snapshot was empty despite the direct post-restart command showing httpd listening on TCP 8080 shortly beforehand; this inconsistency slightly lowers confidence.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation and therefore does not establish final dependency consistency, although the package transaction completed successfully and the resulting service passed functional and reboot tests.
The fixed lifecycle collector cannot report failed SysV services because its failed-service observation only supports systemd.
Requirement document-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations had clear purposes: installing compatible Apache packages, configuring authentication/WebDAV and permissions, enabling startup, exercising bounded tests with cleanup, and performing the mandatory reboot. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up. No abandoned WebDAV test documents were observed.
